occupations.cat: Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians

n.story:
Your role is evolving from a reactive repair person to a high-tech systems diagnostician. While the physical act of crawling through ducts and soldering pipes remains a human domain, the 'brain work' of the job is being supercharged. Instead of manually recording test data or flipping through thick paper manuals to find a specific wiring diagram, you will use Augmented Reality (AR) glasses that overlay digital schematics directly onto the physical equipment you are servicing. AI will analyze sensor data in real-time to predict a failure before it happens, telling you exactly which part to bring to the site.

As you work, AI-powered tools will handle the complex calculations of fluid mechanics and thermodynamics that used to require significant mental effort or specialized engineering consultations. You will spend less time 'guessing' the source of a malfunction and more time performing high-precision physical installations and complex troubleshooting that robots cannot yet replicate in non-standardized environments. You are becoming a 'bionic' technician, where your physical dexterity is guided by immense computational power.
auto: Manual recording and logging of test data
Searching through technical manuals and blueprints
Routine machinery status checks via sensors
Calculating fluid flow and thermal loads
amp: Optimizing system energy efficiency through simulations
Rapid diagnosis of intermittent equipment malfunctions
Precision parameter setting for welding and soldering
tools: AR-based remote assistance and manual overlays
Generative design tools for ductwork and piping
n.adv: Embrace digital literacy and get comfortable with AR and IoT diagnostic tools. Your future value lies in being the physical 'hands' for sophisticated AI diagnostic 'brains,' so master the high-dexterity tasks AI can't touch.
